title: How to build a lead magnet that gives everything away: solve the 'early narrow' problem
summary: Justin Welsh argues that lead magnets which teach 10% and sell 90% feel like a trick and erode trust. Instead, map your customer's journey, pick an early, narrow step that unlocks the rest, solve it completely for free, and then sell the remainder of the journey.

principles.text: Withholding real information in a lead magnet feels like a trick and destroys the trust you've built.
principles.quote: People can tell when you’re holding back the real information and that can feel like a trick. And once people feel tricked? That erodes any trust you’ve built with them.

principles.text: Start by listing every step your customer must get right to reach their big goal, in logical order.
principles.quote: Make a list of everything your ideal customer needs to figure out in order to accomplish their big goal. And then organize your list by the most logical steps.

principles.text: Pick an 'early narrow' problem: a crucial early step that, once solved, unlocks the rest of the journey.
principles.quote: This is a problem that, when solved, unlocks the rest of the ‘wider journey’ for your customer.

principles.text: Solve the narrow problem 100% and give it away generously; you keep your promise and no one is tricked.
principles.quote: Design a lead magnet that 100% solves that narrow problem. And give it all away generously.

principles.text: Solving the first step makes you a trusted guide and the logical choice for the rest of the journey.
principles.quote: You’re now the logical choice to continue working with to get even better. You’ve demonstrated your expertise, helped your potential customer, and built trust early on.

principles.text: Sell the remaining journey at the end of the lead magnet, via a simple video, email series, or inside the magnet itself.
principles.quote: Sell the remainder of the journey in a simple video, email series, or inside of your lead magnet.
